No. The story does not have a balance between scene and summary/exposition; instead, it relies almost entirely on "scene." 

Written in the format of a dramatic script, the entire story unfolds in real-time through dialogue and immediate physical actions (stage directions). There is virtually no narrative summary to compress time, nor is there direct exposition to explain the characters' shared history or what happened "back in March." Instead, all background information is merely hinted at through the subtext of the real-time conversation.
